complexity.correctness_reason: An input containing an empty chain — explicitly permitted, e.g. lists = [[]] from Example 3 — puts None in lists, and the head scan crashes with AttributeError on lists[j].val.
complexity.notes: Dropping the redundant vals array is a nice cleanup — it only ever duplicated lists[i].val. The short-circuit on equal values is sound given the sortedness invariant, but it only pays off when duplicates are common; on inputs with rare ties the scan is Theta(k) per node. Two fragilities: the code indexes lists[j].val without checking for None, and the sentinel ListNode(-10000) hardcodes the statement's value floor — any node valued below -10000 would be emitted out of order. A O(n log k) solution exists via ||a min-heap over the k chain heads|| or ||pairwise divide-and-conquer merging of the chains||, which would be O(n log n) on this ladder.
complexity.summary: Repeatedly scans every remaining chain head for the minimum value (short-circuiting when a head equals the last emitted value), splices that node onto the output list, and rewires the input chains in place. With the scaling ladder's k = sqrt(n) chains and rare ties, each of the n selections costs Theta(k).
